candidates.passage: In terms of EV, the business finally is on track. I am happy to share that the EV business is gradually picking up and close this year with a revenue of INR 20 crores. We are expecting now to double this revenue in the current financial year.
candidates.speaker: Jayant Davar (Executive Chairman & CEO)
candidates.adjudication_note: EV sub-segment. Base FY26 = INR 20 cr, so ~INR 40 cr FY27. Corroborated by Jayant on page 19 ('going from a INR 20 crore revenue to a INR 40 crore revenue') and Yashpal on page 6 ('revenues to approximately double'). Segment-level -> not scorable.

candidates.passage: Sandhar is on a growth path, and I would like to further reiterate that we expect to double our revenues every three to four years with consistent improvements in margins and return on investments.
candidates.speaker: Jayant Davar (Executive Chairman & CEO)
candidates.adjudication_note: PRIMARY long-horizon re-rating signal. Stated as a 2x multiple, no firm target year -> inferred FY29-FY30 (3-4 yrs from FY26). Implied ~19-26% CAGR; analyst Chirag (page 5) computed '20-25% annualized'. Absolute equivalent surfaces explicitly as 'INR 10,000 crores' on page 12 (candidate 17). FY26 base revenue INR 4,852 cr. Reaffirmed by Yashpal (pages 9, 12) and Jayant (page 12).

candidates.passage: This particular year will be another very interesting year, and despite all the problems in the polycrisis that I spoke about, I do expect that even on a conservative level, I am happy to give a guidance of over a 15% growth in the overall revenue. This is without taking a price retrigger, which is likely to happen, especially with a lot of costs having gone up, a lot of states announcing new power costs, which has also been a challenge in the last few months.
candidates.speaker: Jayant Davar (Executive Chairman & CEO)
candidates.adjudication_note: Stated as a FLOOR ('over 15%'), explicitly excluding pricing-retrigger upside. Company-level consolidated revenue growth, near-term -> scorable. Refined to '15-16% plus' on page 5 (candidate 4). FY26 base INR 4,852 cr.

candidates.passage: We will, of course, have to wait and see, and therefore that is the reason why I am giving you a conservative estimate of 15% plus, 15% to 16% plus of revenue growth this year. This, of course, doesn't include the pricing retrigger that I spoke about, which will bring additional revenue to the company.
candidates.speaker: Jayant Davar (Executive Chairman & CEO)
candidates.adjudication_note: Near-duplicate of candidate 3 with a tighter band ('15% to 16% plus'). Dedup decision for the human: keep one as canonical FY27 revenue-growth GT, or keep both. Same ex-pricing-retrigger caveat.

candidates.passage: Sure, sir. So, as we have mentioned on page 7 also of our investor presentation, one of the lossmaking units is Sundaram-Clayton's business that we have acquired in March 25. The shifting is in progress and I think by the end of Quarter 2, we would be able to shift the entire business to our own premises. I think from Quarter 3 onwards, we will start a turnaround in the units with our new EBT levels. But on a yearly basis, '26-'27, we expect to continue with EBT level losses in this die-casting business that we acquired from Sundaram-Clayton.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Two binary events bundled: (a) shift to own premises by end Q2 FY27; (b) turnaround 'starts' Q3 FY27 BUT full-year FY27 still expected at EBT-level loss. Important nuance: the unit does NOT reach full-year profit in FY27. Jayant restates 'Sundaram-Clayton... turn around in Quarter 3' on page 10.

candidates.passage: There is another project in Khed City for aluminum die-casting, which is focused on passenger vehicle segment. From Quarter 2 onwards, it will start generating EBT level margins. So, this is a turnaround time for this project.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Binary: Khed City aluminium die-casting turns EBT-positive from Q2 FY27. Restated by Jayant on page 10 ('Khed City in Quarter 2').

candidates.passage: There is another project in Pune, cabins and fabrication. That also we expect to start turnaround from the end of Quarter 2 of this current financial year.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Binary: Pune cabins-and-fabrication turnaround by end Q2 FY27. Likely the same facility Jayant calls 'Sanaswadi in Quarter 2' on page 10 (Sanaswadi is in the Pune belt) - verify whether Pune and Sanaswadi are one project or two.

candidates.passage: And then EV business, we expect to turnaround in profitability in FY '28, means the next financial year. This year, we expect the revenues to approximately double, but there would be losses again as we are trying to develop more new products also and capturing new markets. So, that involves some cost.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Binary: EV business turns profitable in FY28 (~2 yrs out -> medium). Note FY27 stays loss-making despite revenue doubling (the revenue-double itself is candidate 1). Restated by Jayant page 10 ('EV business we are saying Financial Year '28').

candidates.passage: And Romania also, FY '28, we are expecting to go at a break-even or I would say in a profitability mode. So, this is how the timelines as the management expects while we sit on today's timeline.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Binary: Romania overseas operation breakeven/profitability in FY28. Level could be tagged 'geography' (overseas subsidiary) instead of 'segment' - human to decide convention. Restated by Jayant page 10 ('Romania in Financial Year '28').

candidates.passage: I just want to add here, Chirag, you mentioned that we made an investment in these 5 units to a level of INR 342 crores, which has generated a revenue of INR 468 crores. So, if I was to add these businesses, this particular financial year, the investment will mean a revenue from INR 468 crores, INR 342 crores would convert itself into maybe 2.5x in this year itself.
candidates.speaker: Jayant Davar (Executive Chairman & CEO)
candidates.adjudication_note: INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT - scrutinise. '2.5x' is asset turnover on INR 342 cr investment (=> ~INR 855 cr) but also framed against the INR 468 cr current revenue. Yashpal then revises to INR 700-750 cr and '2x to 2.5x' on page 10 (candidate 16). Same underlying guidance as candidate 16; pick a value/range. Segment-level (5 new-project units) -> not scorable.

candidates.passage: Yes, absolutely. Absolutely. So, if you saw a breakeven, the idea was to breakeven in the last quarter, which we had promised everyone we will and we have. The idea is to improve from there on and go into positive territory at the EBT level. So, we were zero at the EBT level. We want to improve on the EBT level going forward.
candidates.speaker: Jayant Davar (Executive Chairman & CEO)
candidates.adjudication_note: BORDERLINE Gate 1 timeframe - 'going forward' has no firm endpoint (cf. the prompt's borderline example). Breakeven itself already happened (Q4 FY26, backward-looking). Forward content = move from zero EBT into positive territory, with a flagged Q1 FY27 dip from aluminium lag. Verify whether this clears the timeframe gate; if cut, the substantive overseas signal is already implied. Level arguably 'geography'.

candidates.passage: And in the earlier calls, our Chairman has mentioned that we keep our CapEx limited to 5% to 7% of our revenues. So, taking our 15% growth on the current year's revenue, which is roughly INR 5,500 crores, you can expect somehow capital outlay of INR 275 crores to around INR 310 crores for the upcoming financial year, which will include a part of growth CapEx, part of maintenance CapEx, part of upgradation CapEx required to upgrade our some old facilities also.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: FY27 capex INR 275-310 cr. capex_absolute -> always non-scorable. Same sentence also yields the FY27 revenue figure (candidate 13).

candidates.passage: So, taking our 15% growth on the current year's revenue, which is roughly INR 5,500 crores, you can expect somehow capital outlay of INR 275 crores to around INR 310 crores for the upcoming financial year...
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Absolute expression of the FY27 15% revenue-growth guidance (candidates 3/4). Note 4,852 x 1.15 = ~5,580; management rounded to 'roughly INR 5,500 crores'. Company-level, near -> scorable. Decide whether to keep as a separate absolute GT item or fold into the growth-% item.

candidates.passage: And like as we discussed and we discussed in earlier calls also, every year we want to grow and improve our EBITDA levels by at least half a percent, in a range of half a percent, which could be 0.20, 0.30 or something like that. So, this year also we are expecting to improve our EBITDA margins in a range of half a percent, which could be 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, depending on the market dynamics as far as addressed in the previous question.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: DELTA, not an absolute target - improve margin by ~0.1-0.5 pp this year. Meets all four scorable gates on paper (company, EBITDA margin, near, Screener-matchable), so tagged scorable=true, BUT: (a) it is a delta - consider renaming other_ebitda_margin_delta so eval doesn't read it as an absolute; (b) candidate 15 reveals the 0.25 pp improvement is EXCLUDING new projects, and consolidated FY27 margin may be roughly flat due to new-project commissioning drag. Resolve scorability + naming here. FY26 baseline: full-year EBITDA margin ~10.6%; Q4 exit cited as 10.57-11.08% (transcript inconsistent).

candidates.passage: Saket Kapoor: ...in particular, the margin should grow from this 10.57 level to a band of 0.25 to 0.5. That should be the understanding as of now. [...] Yashpal Jain: ...excluding the new projects that would be coming up, yes we could expect a growth of 0.25% in EBITDA margins. But at the same time the new projects, these would be in the commercial production and new projects will be coming up during the current financial.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Analyst-framed (0.25-0.5 pp from 10.57), management accepts 0.25 pp but ONLY 'excluding the new projects'. Tagged scorable=false because the ex-new-projects figure is not the consolidated number Screener reports -> not cleanly matchable. Near-duplicate of candidate 14; together they imply consolidated FY27 margin = roughly flat to +0.5 pp. Adjudicate as one margin item.

candidates.passage: Ashutosh Tiwari: So, this INR 468 crore revenue that you did in this year can go to INR 800 crore plus in FY '27? [...] Yashpal Jain: 2.5% you can say INR 700 crores, INR 750 crores something. I mean, it is a range sir has given. 2.5x, which can be 2x to 2.5x basically, I would say. So, around INR 750 crores of revenue these projects can do. 468 they have already delivered.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Absolute version of candidate 10's '2.5x'. Note the math is inconsistent: 2.5x of 468 = ~1,170 cr, yet Yashpal lands on INR 700-750 cr and hedges '2x to 2.5x'; analyst floated INR 800 cr+. New-project (segment) revenue -> not scorable. Reconcile value with candidate 10; likely keep as a single new-projects FY27 revenue GT item.

candidates.passage: Yes, sure. So, like, Aditya, sir has mentioned, three to four years, we want to double our revenue. So, in case we touch INR 10,000 crores or more, we would expect that our return on capital employed sees improvement because we are more focusing on return on capital employed as the volumes will go up because the percent of margin is a limiting factor for us in terms of EBITDA and EBT.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Absolute form of the 'double every 3-4 years' aspiration (candidate 2): 4,852 -> ~10,000 cr = one doubling. No firm year stated; analyst Aditya framed 'end of FY30 or 31'; doubling cadence implies FY29-FY30. Verify the target year you assign. Long-horizon, company-level -> not scorable, but a PRIMARY re-rating/ambition signal.

candidates.passage: So, in that scenario, you can expect that on a INR 10,000 crores of revenue, we could be in a position to generate a PAT of around INR 450 crores, something around that, to achieve that return on capital employed. This is how we expect.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Long-horizon PAT target tied to the INR 10,000 cr revenue scenario. FY26 PAT base = INR 199 cr (so ~2.3x). Jayant explicitly endorses on page 12: 'the number that Yashpalji has given you of INR 450 crores seems quite safe'. Same timeline uncertainty as candidate 17. Long horizon -> not scorable.

candidates.passage: But we are targeting an improvement return on capital employed starting with a post-tax return of 15%, going something at a highest peak of 20%.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Post-tax ROCE target tied to the INR 10,000 cr scenario. Inconsistency to resolve: stated '15% ... peak of 20%' here, but restated as '18% to 20% post-tax' on the same page (in candidate 20's passage). Also distinguish from the existing-business '20% ROCE threshold' Chirag cited (page 5), which is a different/current metric. ROCE not in scorable P&L set + long horizon -> not scorable.

candidates.passage: EBITDA, as you know, that we, I mean, manufacturing diversified products of die casting, locks and mirrors, I mean, assembly as well as the manufacturing. So, while EBITDA levels will remain constant around 11%, but with the volumes coming up and the revenue going up, automatically in terms of absolute returns, our multiplier will be giving us a more return on capital employed. So, more of a cash with us in that terms. So, at that point of time, the percent margins won't be of much importance in terms of EBITDA or EBT. And more focus would be on how to generate more absolute margins. And the focus going forward is again on ROE and ROCE, basically. So, even if at the EBITDA of 11%, you can take on INR 10,000 crores close to having INR 1100 crores, expect to return levels of 18% to 20% post-tax.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Long-run EBITDA margin held ~constant at 11% at the INR 10,000 cr scale (implies ~INR 1,100 cr EBITDA absolute). Notable contrast with the near-term +0.25-0.5 pp improvement (candidates 14/15) - long-run framing is margin-flat, returns driven by volume/ROCE. Long horizon -> not scorable; feeds the ambition layer, not credibility.

candidates.passage: So, I mean, the term loans are INR 384 crores, which will be automatically paid with the due schedules. This year we have a repayment commitment of around close to INR 103 crores with various banks.
candidates.speaker: Yashpal Jain (CFO & Company Secretary)
candidates.adjudication_note: Scheduled FY27 term-debt repayment ~INR 103 cr (a forward commitment with number + date; passes Gate 1 structurally). Borderline as 'guidance' vs scheduled obligation - keep if you want debt-trajectory signals, cut if GT is performance-only. Not a scorable P&L metric. The accompanying 'term loans pair down in next 3-4 years' has no figure -> excluded.

candidates.passage: We are already in the process. I am not at liberty to say, but we have identified some prospective partners who should be able to give us the technology that we seek. But of course, the finalization of that, we need the go ahead from the customers who like G. J. just said, the customers have it under consideration. We are having discussions. And as soon as we can lock in the kind of technology that is apt and is attributable to the Indian industry, we will lock it with that particular corresponding partner and take that to the market within the next 12 months.
candidates.speaker: Jayant Davar (Executive Chairman & CEO)
candidates.adjudication_note: Binary go-to-market event (telematics/new-tech via tech-transfer) within 12 months of the call. CONDITIONAL ('as soon as we can lock in ... we will'), and contingent on customer go-ahead -> verify whether the conditionality weakens it below Gate 1. Level could be 'segment' (new product line).
